posts.title: Speed Simulator 2 is out
posts.body: Speed Simulator 2 is a whole new game, not an update to the original. Fly out through four ring-shaped regions, break each speed gate to get in, and collect orbs to level up and buy upgrades. Fly greedily in the wild regions and the Wraith comes for you, so you'll have to outrun it. There are ten ships to unlock, each with its own wake and ability, plus three Halloween ships for anyone who plays during the event. Your progress saves to your Alloy account from the first flight, and the original Speed Simulator and its saves are untouched.

posts.title: Tomorrowless replaces Flytale
posts.body: Flytale has made way for Tomorrowless, a new pixel RPG from the same team. It is always 11:59 in Hushwood, and midnight never comes: spare or fight your way through the town, find out why the clock stopped, and face bosses whose attacks break out of the box. Four routes, four endings. Old Flytale links now take you straight to it.

posts.title: Madballs: twenty new levels and a new look
posts.body: Madballs grows to 34 levels with a fresh coat of paint across the board. The transcendent skin is now called Atlas, with a reworked World Flip and a new trail, and ball trails no longer freeze in mid-air after a shot. Your coins, skins, unlocked levels and best scores carry over, on this device and on your Alloy account.

posts.title: Umbra's ultimates come to life
posts.body: Every body in Umbra's cutscenes now moves between its key poses: fighters knocked flying roll and flail, every hit lands as a recoil, landings give, and anyone standing still breathes and shifts their weight. The same layer runs in regular fights on hits, knockdowns and throws. Several ultimates were re-choreographed so no shot reads as a sliding picture any more - Rin's is now a real barrage of thrusts at different heights, Goliath lifts you by the throat before the slam, and every big hit follows through instead of freezing. Dashes push off and stride, and back dashes crouch, hop and land. A follow-up fix keeps one guest's spinning sphere in his palm as he dives, instead of it appearing on the target before he arrives. One more small fix followed later the same day.

posts.title: Two more guest fighters in Umbra
posts.body: Umbra has two new limited-time guests, available from today until 15 November. Each has a path of their own: clear it while the event runs and that fighter is yours to keep, saved to your Alloy account and still there after the event ends. The earlier two guests are still around too - the first one leaves on 26 October.

posts.title: Redwater gets a new look
posts.body: Redwater has been redrawn from the ground up in a three-quarter view: characters with outfits and animation, all 20 guns redrawn with new shooting effects, lit terrain, flowing water and proper night lighting. The river no longer runs through the Calloway homestead, and there are now four bridges wherever a road or the railway crosses it. Two story jobs that never started now do, kill jobs count properly, bounties are easier, and a long list of smaller bugs is gone - the full list is in the update log. Your save carries straight over, and saves that were stuck in the story move on by themselves.

posts.title: Every game is on Alloy now
posts.body: The last three games have moved over. Echoes keeps the tracks you've recovered and your best clear times, and Cosmic Climb keeps your best altitude and best score, both synced to your Alloy account. Flytale gets the check against unofficial copies; every visit starts at Chapter 1, so there is nothing to save. That completes the move: fourteen games save to your account, all twenty refuse to run as copies on other sites, and the next step is the first limited-time events.

posts.title: Hardburn saves to your Alloy account
posts.body: Your Hardburn credits, scrap, airframe collection, pity counters and personal bests on every course now sync to your Alloy account, so your hangar follows you to any device. Sign in and the progress already in this browser uploads the first time. Hardburn also reports targets destroyed to Alloy events.

posts.title: Port Vesper and Madballs join Alloy accounts
posts.body: Port Vesper now keeps your money, respect, weapons, properties and contract perks on your Alloy account, and Madballs keeps your coins, skin collection, unlocked levels and best scores. Sign in and the progress already in this browser uploads the first time. Port Vesper also closes three money loops that could be farmed forever - sleeping is once a day, bar tips once a minute, and owned cars sell at resale price. Rats With Wings and Elementalis get the check against unofficial copies; every round and every run in them starts fresh, so there is nothing to save.

posts.title: Umbra: limited-time guest fighters, saved to your account
posts.body: Umbra's story mode has made way for special fighters. The first two are limited-time guests: each one is playable while their event runs, and clearing their path during the event keeps them for good. Your wins, cleared paths and kept guests now sync to your Alloy account, so a guest you earned is still yours on any device, even after the event ends.

posts.title: Foil & Fortune and Abyssal Dredging join Alloy accounts
posts.body: Your card shop and your dredging rig now sync to your Alloy account. In Foil & Fortune that means your cash, binder, graded slabs, vault, staff and upgrades; in Abyssal Dredging your cargo, upgrades, Pressure Cores, Descents and Collection. Sign in and the progress already in this browser uploads the first time. Both games also report to Alloy events. Sole & Co. and Aura Fighters get the check against unofficial copies; neither keeps anything between visits, so there is nothing to save.

posts.title: Multiverse Fighters becomes Umbra
posts.body: Multiverse Fighters has been rebuilt from scratch as Umbra, a duel of shadows: eight fighters in pure black silhouette, each lit by a single colour, with cinematic ultimates, blocking high and low, throws and cancels. Play the CPU at four difficulties, a friend on one keyboard, or the training dummy. Old links to Multiverse Fighters now take you straight to Umbra.

posts.title: Fixed: the account button kept loading
posts.body: If you were signed in, the account button in the top right could stay on its loading shimmer forever after opening a page, even though your account was working underneath. It now shows your player name as soon as sign-in finishes.

posts.title: A new look, built from the logo
posts.body: The site has been redesigned around the Alloy Studios logo: polished chrome, warm copper light and a brushed-metal finish, with the real logo in the header, a slow glint across the masthead and cards that catch the light as you move over them. Every animation switches off if your device is set to reduce motion. The front page also keeps just the latest news now; older posts are one click away.

posts.title: Four more games save to your Alloy account
posts.body: Neon Survivor Legends, Meridian, Rank Zero and Redwater now sync to your Alloy account, so your upgrades, skins, levels and story progress follow you to any device. Sign in with the button at the top of the page. Progress you already have in this browser is uploaded the first time you do. Every save is checked on our server first, so nobody can skip the grind with DevTools. Grand Line also gets the new check against unofficial copies; it doesn't need saving, because every voyage starts fresh.

posts.title: Speed Simulator is fully on Alloy accounts
posts.body: Speed Simulator now saves through your Alloy account like Orbit Dash, and its old login is gone for good. If you played before, your progress was carried over, and it comes across the first time you sign in, even if that's months from now. The game also loads faster now, because it no longer fetches part of itself from a server.

posts.title: Only the real thing
posts.body: Some sites show browser games inside their own pages, wrapped in their ads, or copy them outright. Every page here now notices when it's been embedded somewhere else and points you back to alloy-studios.github.io instead. Orbit Dash also refuses to run as a copy on another site; the rest of the games get the same check as they move to Alloy accounts. If a game ever says you're on an unofficial copy, its button takes you to the real one - free, with your progress saved to your account.

posts.title: New contact address
posts.body: Alloy Studios can now be reached at alloy-studios@googlegroups.com - it goes straight to the whole team. The old alloystudiocontact address no longer works, so please don't send anything there.

posts.title: Alloy accounts are rolling out
posts.body: There is now a Sign in button at the top of every page. One Alloy account works in every game, so progress follows you between devices instead of living in one browser. Orbit Dash is the first game on it; the rest of the catalogue moves over one at a time. Speed Simulator players: your existing login carries over, and so does your progress. Every save is checked on our server before it's kept, and accounts are what will power limited-time events.

posts.title: Counting visits, without cookies
posts.body: The site now keeps simple visit counts with GoatCounter, so we can see which games people actually find. It uses no cookies and collects no personal data - just page views, referring sites and rough location - which is also why there is no consent popup.

posts.title: Every game has a real thumbnail
posts.body: The generated colour tiles are gone. Every card in the library now shows a frame rendered from the game itself - staged mid-play, no text, built to still read at card size. Alloy Mind has also been retired from the catalogue.

posts.title: Every game in the catalogue is now reworked
posts.body: Hardburn and Rats With Wings arrive, replacing Anime Survivors and Neon Defense Grid. Echoes is rebuilt from scratch with three new tracks, Abyssal Dredging gets a real ocean under the rig, and Sole & Co. fixes the economy bug that made it unwinnable. Orbit Dash closes it out, rebuilt as an 18th-century brass orrery printed on cyanotype paper. That is the whole library caught up.

posts.title: Redwater arrives, four more games reworked
posts.body: Redwater replaces the old Blue Lock game outright - a top-down open-world western RPG where you ride in with no side and leave with one. Rivalforge is now Meridian - new name, new URL at /meridian/, and moved from a night-shift machine hall to high noon, with two new skin tiers and a reworked economy. Aura Fighters, Flytale and Multiverse Fighters are rebuilt too. Six games left on their original build.

posts.title: Seven games fully reworked
posts.body: Blox Fruits 2D is now Grand Line, a top-down pirate action-RPG, and Solo Leveling is now Rank Zero: Sovereign Protocol, fought on the page of an open book. Port Vesper, Neon Speed Simulator, Foil & Fortune, Cosmic Climb and Elementalis have all been rebuilt too. Open the full update log for what changed in each.

posts.title: Elementalis and Sole & Co. are live
posts.body: Two new games. Elementalis is a spellcasting action-RPG across the Broken Wilds, with a Grimoire for mastering and fusing elements. Sole & Co. is a sneaker shop sim - you inherit a two-metre-wide shop, three pairs and $1,500, and have to make rent.

posts.title: Three games added, contact address changed
posts.body: Multiverse Fighters, Flytale and Madballs join the catalogue, Alloy Mind gets a proper write-up, and Rivalforge and Neon Survivor Legends are updated to their latest builds.

posts.title: Rivalforge overhaul
posts.body: Rivalforge gets its biggest update yet in the calibration bay. Chain multipliers, optics calibration and a reworked scoring pass.

posts.title: Alloy Studios is live
posts.body: Every game now lives at one address, with one shared player: fullscreen, restart, and search across the whole library. Old per-game links redirect to their new home.
